semanticHomePolicy.definition: Folder token and local folder context may contribute Semantic Home evidence.
semanticHomePolicy.derivationMeaning: May support Semantic Home derivation when combined with lineage and other bounded evidence.
semanticHomePolicy.guardrails: Evidence only; not final placement truth and not Naming ownership.

semanticHomePolicy.definition: Parent chain context may contribute nested semantic interpretation evidence.
semanticHomePolicy.derivationMeaning: May inform nested Semantic Home interpretation through lineage relationships. How Tree uses this evidence is defined by the Tree specification (Stage 2 S2.10 RR2); broader contextual reasoning over parent and sibling structure is a possible future use that requires a contract amendment.
semanticHomePolicy.guardrails: Evidence only; not final placement truth and not Structural Home identity by itself.

semanticHomePolicy.definition: Naming bridge outputs may contribute semantic-name or semantic-family evidence.
semanticHomePolicy.derivationMeaning: May support Semantic Home derivation only through bounded bridge interpretation inside Tree-owned advisory reasoning.
semanticHomePolicy.guardrails: Naming retains ownership of semantic-name and semantic-family interpretation; this lane consumes bounded evidence only.

semanticHomePolicy.definition: Structural Home context may contribute boundary evidence around candidate semantic interpretation.
semanticHomePolicy.derivationMeaning: May provide context and corroboration for candidate semantic interpretation without becoming Semantic Home truth by itself. How Tree uses this evidence is defined by the Tree specification (Stage 2 S2.10 RR2: under the current contract it is corroboration only and does not change eligibility); any stronger role requires a contract amendment.
semanticHomePolicy.guardrails: Structural Home identity remains separately owned and must not be replaced by Semantic Home guidance.

semanticHomePolicy.definition: Structural-home signal policy outputs may provide weak or contextual boundary evidence.
semanticHomePolicy.derivationMeaning: Must remain bounded as supporting evidence and must not become standalone Semantic Home truth.
semanticHomePolicy.guardrails: Does not replace structural-home signal policy registry ownership and remains evidence only.

semanticHomePolicy.definition: Repo-top structural-home context may provide boundary evidence for semantic interpretation.
semanticHomePolicy.derivationMeaning: May provide context around semantic interpretation but must not become canonical Semantic Home truth. How Tree uses this evidence is defined by the Tree specification (Stage 2 S2.10 RR2: under the current contract Stage 2 does not read it, so it gates no decision); any use requires a contract amendment.
semanticHomePolicy.guardrails: Repo-top structural-home evidence remains Tree-owned and does not replace Naming semantic interpretation.

semanticHomeParameters.rationale: At least half of a candidate's decision members must have usable comparison evidence. Placed between structural-addressing (0.45, intended undetermined) and naming (0.61, intended to pass) by intended outcomes, not by a repository optimum (Tree spec Stage 2 S2.10; calculogic-validator#102 D4, D7).

Two distinct supporting occurrences make the smallest observable grouping; one matching file is a relationship, not yet a grouping. Synthetic evidence only: no repository candidate has one to three matches (Tree spec Stage 2 S2.10; calculogic-validator#102 D5, D7).

Symmetric with eligible-share, leaving an explicitly undecided middle band; also the significance bar for the alternative root reading of a compound label. Synthetic evidence only (Tree spec Stage 2 S2.3, S2.10; calculogic-validator#102 D1, D6, D7).

Symmetric support-share band (not-eligible-share = 1 - eligible-share) with an undecided middle. Symmetry is a policy choice, not a mathematical necessity; the full catalogue supports it (Tree spec Stage 2 S2.10; calculogic-validator#102 D6, D7).
